ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الشَّيْطَانُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ الْحَقِّ وَوَعَدْتُكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُكُمْ وَمَا كَانَ لِي عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِلَّا أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ فَاسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِي فَلَا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ مَا أَنَا بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ وَمَا أَنْتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ إِنِّي كَفَرْتُ بِمَا أَشْرَكْتُمُونِي مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (٢٢)).
The Exalted's saying (إِلَّا أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ): a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because his calling was not a sulṭān, i.e. a proof.
(بِمُصْرِخِيَّ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ. It is the plural of مُصْرِخٍ; the first yāʾ is the yāʾ of the plural and the second is the pronoun of the first person. It was given fatḥa so that the kasra and the yāʾ would not come together after two kasras.
It is also read with kasra on it, and that is weak because of the heaviness we mentioned. There are two views on it:
The first: it was given kasra according to the original form.
The second: he intended by it مُصْرِخِيِّ, and this is a minor dialect (lughayya), whose speakers say فِي and رَمَيْتِيهِ, so that a yāʾ follows the kasra by way of lengthening (ishbāʿ); except that in the verse the final yāʾ was dropped, the kasra before it sufficing.
(بِمَا أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it means الَّذِي (that which); on this view the implied wording is بِالَّذِي أَشْرَكْتُمُونِي بِهِ, i.e. "in the idol, in which you obeyed me as you obeyed it", and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) was dropped. The second: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "in your associating me with Allah, Mighty and Majestic".
And (مِنْ قَبْلُ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَشْرَكْتُمُونِي, i.e. "I now disbelieve in that with which you associated me before".
It is also said that it is attached to كَفَرْتُ, i.e. "I disbelieved before your associating (me), so I will not benefit you at all".

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأُدْخِلَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ تَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيهَا سَلَامٌ (٢٣)).
The Exalted's saying (وَأُدْخِلَ): it is read in the form of the past verb, and it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to بَرَزُوا, or to فَقَالَ الضُّعَفَاءُ. It is also read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with ḍamma on the lām, as an imperfect verb, the fāʿil (agent) being Allah.
(بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ): it may belong to the completion of (أُدْخِلَ), or it may belong to the completion of «خَالِدِينَ».
(تَحِيَّتُهُمْ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) may be annexed to its agent, i.e. they greet one another with this word; or it may be annexed to its object, i.e. Allah, or the angels, greet them.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ وَفَرْعُهَا فِي السَّمَاءِ (٢٤)).
The Exalted's saying (كَلِمَةً): a badal (substitute) for «مَثَلًا». (كَشَجَرَةٍ): a naʿt (adjective) for it. It is also read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, «كَلِمَةٌ» in the nominative, with كَشَجَرَةٍ as its khabar (predicate).
And (تُؤْتِي أُكُلَهَا): a naʿt for the tree; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the meaning of the second clause, i.e. "it rises, yielding its fruit".

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ اجْتُثَّتْ مِنْ فَوْقِ الْأَرْضِ مَا لَهَا مِنْ قَرَارٍ (٢٦)).
The Exalted's saying (مَا لَهَا مِنْ قَرَارٍ): the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) for شَجَرَةٍ. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «اجْتُثَّتْ».

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ وَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الظَّالِمِينَ وَيَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ (٢٧)).
The Exalted's saying (فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُثَبِّتُ. It may also be attached to الثَّابِتِ.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ بَدَّلُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ كُفْرًا وَأَحَلُّوا قَوْمَهُمْ دَارَ الْبَوَارِ (٢٨)).
The Exalted's saying (كُفْرًا): the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of بَدَّلَ.
And (جَهَنَّمَ): a badal (substitute) for دَارِ الْبَوَارِ. It may also be accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. "they will roast in جَهَنَّمَ", or "they will enter جَهَنَّمَ".
And (يَصْلَوْنَهَا) is an explanation (tafsīr) of it; on this view يَصْلَوْنَهَا has no grammatical position. On the first view, its position may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from جَهَنَّمَ, or from الدَّار, or from قَوْمَهُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لِعِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خِلَالٌ (٣١))
The Exalted's saying (يُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ): there are three views on it. The first: it is the answer (jawāb) of «قُلْ», and there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "say to them 'perform the prayer', and they will perform it", i.e. "if you say to them, they will perform it". Al-Akhfash said this.
A group rejected it, saying: because the Messenger's saying (this) to them does not necessitate that they perform (it). In my view this does not invalidate his position, because he did not mean by "the servants" the disbelievers but the believers; and when the Messenger says to them "perform the prayer", they perform it. This is shown by His saying «لِعِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا».
The second position is reported from al-Mubarrad: that the implied wording is "say to them 'perform', they will perform"; so the explicit يُقِيمُوا is the answer to the omitted أَقِيمُوا. A number (of scholars) reported it without addressing its invalidity; and it is invalid for two reasons:
The first: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) differs from the condition, either in the verb or in the agent or in both. When it is the same as it in both the verb and the agent, that is an error, as in your saying قُمْ تَقُمْ ("stand, you will stand"); and the implied wording according to what is mentioned in this view is: "if they perform, they will perform". The second reason: the implied imperative is for direct address (second person), while يُقِيمُوا is in the form of the third person (absence), and that is an error when the agent is one and the same. The third position: it is jussive (majzūm) by an omitted lām, its implied form being لِيُقِيمُوا ("let them perform"), so it is a resumptive (new) command; and the dropping of the lām is permitted because «قُلْ» indicates the command.
And (يُنْفِقُوا) is like يُقِيمُوا.
(سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْفُلْكَ لِتَجْرِيَ فِي الْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْأَنْهَارَ (٣٣)).
[Translator's note: the source entry is numbered for verse 32 but quotes part of verse 32 with the verse marker (٣٣), and the word commented on, دَائِبَيْنِ, is from verse 33.]
The Exalted's saying (دَائِبَيْنِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the sun and the moon.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَآتَاكُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ وَإِنْ تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَظَلُومٌ كَفَّارٌ (٣٤)).
The Exalted's saying (مِنْ كُلِّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ): it is read with «كُلِّ» annexed to «مَا». Then, according to al-Akhfash, مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida); and according to Sībawayh the object is omitted, its implied form being: "of everything you asked Him, what you asked Him".
And (مَا) may mean الَّذِي (that which), or be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), or be maṣdariyya, the maṣdar then having the sense of the object. It is also read with tanwīn on «كُلِّ»; on this reading مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of آتَاكُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذَا الْبَلَدَ آمِنًا وَاجْنُبْنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَنْ نَعْبُدَ الْأَصْنَامَ (٣٥)).
The Exalted's saying (آمِنًا): the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «الْبَلَدَ» is a description of the first object.
And (اجْنُبْنِي): one says جَنَبْتُهُ, أَجْنَبْتُهُ and جَنَّبْتُهُ (I kept him away).
It has been read with a disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) and kasra on the nūn.
(أَنْ نَعْبُدَ): i.e. عَنْ أَنْ نَعْبُدَ ("from worshipping"); the disagreement about its position in the i'rab has been mentioned several times.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ فَمَنْ تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي وَمَنْ عَصَانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٣٦)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمَنْ عَصَانِي): a conditional in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ»; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "to him". Its like was mentioned in (Surat) Yūsuf.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبَّنَا إِنِّي أَسْكَنْتُ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ عِنْدَ بَيْتِكَ الْمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ وَارْزُقْهُمْ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ (٣٧)).
The Exalted's saying (مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي): the object is omitted, i.e. "some offspring of my offspring"; and according to the view of al-Akhfash it may be explained with «مِنْ» as redundant (zāʾida).
(عِنْدَ بَيْتِكَ): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) for «وَادٍ», or a badal (substitute) for it. (لِيُقِيمُوا): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَسْكَنْتُ. And (تَهْوِي) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of اجْعَلْ.
It is read with kasra on the wāw, and its past is هَوِيَ and its maṣdar (verbal noun) الْهَوَى. It is also read with fatḥa on the wāw followed by an alif, and its past is هَوِيَ يَهْوَى هَوًى. [Translator's note: the source gives هَوِيَ as the past for both readings; for the first reading (تَهْوِي) one would expect هَوَى يَهْوِي. Translated as written.] The two meanings are close, except that هَوَى is transitive by itself while هَوِيَ is transitive with إِلَى; however, the second reading was made transitive with إِلَى by treating it like تَمِيلُ ("inclines").

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي وَهَبَ لِي عَلَى الْكِبَرِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ (٣٩)).
The Exalted's saying (عَلَى الْكِبَرِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ in «وَهَبَ لِي».

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ (٤٠)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the object in «اجْعَلْنِي», and the implied wording is: "and (make) of my offspring one who performs the prayer".

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ غَافِلًا عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ الظَّالِمُونَ إِنَّمَا يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ الْأَبْصَارُ (٤٢)).
The Exalted's saying (إِنَّمَا يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ): it is read with nūn (نُؤَخِّرُهُمْ, "We defer them") as an expression of majesty, and with yāʾ because the name of Allah the Exalted comes before it.
(لِيَوْمٍ): i.e. for the sake of the recompense of a day. It is also said that it means إِلَى ("until").

ukberi-tibyan:43-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ لَا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَوَاءٌ (٤٣) وَأَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ الْعَذَابُ فَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا رَبَّنَا أَخِّرْنَا إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ نُجِبْ دَعْوَتَكَ وَنَتَّبِعِ الرُّسُلَ أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوا أَقْسَمْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ زَوَالٍ (٤٤)).
The Exalted's saying (مُهْطِعِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْأَبْصَارِ. This is permitted only because the implied wording is "on which the owners of the eyes stare", since one says شَخَصَ زَيْدٌ بَصَرَهُ ("Zayd fixed his gaze"); or (because) the eyes point to their owners, so the ḥāl was made from what is pointed to. It may also be the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "you see them مُهْطِعِينَ (hastening)".
(مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ): the annexation (iḍāfa) is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa), because it (the participle) refers to the future or the present. (لَا يَرْتَدُّ): a ḥāl from the pronoun in مُقْنِعِي, or a badal (substitute) for مُقْنِعِي. And (طَرْفُهُمْ) is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of the agent, because one says مَا طَرَفَتْ عَيْنُهُ ("his eye did not blink") and لَمْ يَبْقَ عَيْنٌ تَطْرُفُ ("no eye remained blinking"); and it has come in the plural. And (وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَوَاءٌ) is a clause in the position of the ḥāl as well; so the governor (ʿāmil) of the ḥāl may be «يَرْتَدُّ» or whatever governors before it are fit to govern it.
If it is said: how is «هَوَاءٌ» singular when it is the khabar (predicate) of a plural? It is answered: since the meaning of هَوَاء here is "empty, hollowed-out", it was made singular, just as it is permissible to make فَارِغَةٌ ("empty", feminine singular) singular; because the tāʾ of the feminine in it indicates the femininity of the plural in «أَفْئِدَتِهِمْ». Similar to it are أَحْوَالٌ صَعْبَةٌ ("hard states"), أَفْعَالٌ فَاسِدَةٌ ("corrupt deeds") and the like.
(يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ): it is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أَنْذِرْ; the implied wording is "and warn them of the punishment of a day". It may not be an adverb of time (ẓarf), because the warning does not take place on that day.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَسَكَنْتُمْ فِي مَسَاكِنِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ كَيْفَ فَعَلْنَا بِهِمْ وَضَرَبْنَا لَكُمُ الْأَمْثَالَ (٤٥)).
The Exalted's saying (وَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ): its fāʿil (agent) is a concealed pronoun indicated by the context, i.e. "their state became clear to you".
And (كَيْفَ) is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by «فَعَلْنَا». It may not be the fāʿil of «تَبَيَّنَ», for two reasons. The first: an interrogative is not governed by what precedes it. The second: كَيْفَ can only be a khabar (predicate), or a ẓarf (adverbial) or a ḥāl (circumstantial), according to their disagreement on that.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَدْ مَكَرُوا مَكْرَهُمْ وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَكْرُهُمْ وَإِنْ كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبَالُ (٤٦)).
The Exalted's saying (وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَكْرُهُمْ): i.e. the knowledge of their plotting, or the recompense of their plotting; the muḍāf (first term of the construct) was dropped.
(لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ): it is read with kasra on the first lām and fatḥa on the second, and it is the lām of kay (lām of purpose). On this reading there are two views about «إِنْ». The first: it means مَا (negation), i.e. "their plotting was not such as to remove the mountains"; and this is a likening (tamthīl) of the affair of the Prophet ﷺ. The second: it is lightened from the heavy (inna), and the meaning is: they plotted in order to remove what is like the mountains in firmness, and such plotting is futile. It is also read with fatḥa on the first lām and ḍamma on the second (لَتَزُولُ); on this reading إِنْ is lightened from the heavy, and the lām is for emphasis (tawkīd).
It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with fatḥa on both lāms, and that is according to the dialect of those who give fatḥa to the lām of kay. And «كَانَ» here may be the complete (tāmma) one, and it may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقَامٍ (٤٧)).
The Exalted's saying (مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ): الرُّسُل is the first object and الْوَعْد is the second object. The annexation of مُخْلِف to الْوَعْد is a matter of latitude (ittisāʿ); the original is مُخْلِفٌ رُسُلَهُ وَعْدَهُ, but it became acceptable since each of the two is an object. It is close to their saying:
يَا سَارِقَ اللَّيْلَةِ أَهْلَ الدَّارِ
(O you who rob, in the night, the people of the house.)
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ (٤٨)).
The Exalted's saying (يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ): يَوْمَ here is an adverb of time (ẓarf) for «انْتِقَامٍ», or the object of an omitted verb, i.e. "remember the day". It may not be a ẓarf for مُخْلِف nor for وَعْدِهِ, because what comes before إِنَّ does not govern what comes after it; but it is permissible to extract from the meaning of the speech something that governs the ẓarf, i.e. "He does not break His promise on the day (the earth) is changed".
(وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ): its implied form is "and other than the heavens"; it (غَيْر) was dropped because what precedes indicates it.
(وَبَرَزُوا): it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), i.e. "and they will come forth".
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْأَرْض, with «قَدْ» intended along with it.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَرَابِيلُهُمْ مِنْ قَطِرَانٍ وَتَغْشَى وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ (٥٠)).
The Exalted's saying (سَرَابِيلُهُمْ مِنْ قَطِرَانٍ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمُجْرِمِينَ, or from the pronoun in «مُقَرَّنِينَ». The majority take الْقَطِرَان as one word.
It is also read «قِطْرٍ آنٍ» as two words: الْقِطْر is copper, and الْآنِي is that which has reached the utmost heat.
And (تَغْشَى) is also a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَجْزِيَ اللَّهُ كُلَّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ (٥١)).
The Exalted's saying (لِيَجْزِيَ): i.e. "We did that for the sake of recompense"; it may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to بَرَزُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَذَا بَلَاغٌ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيُنْذَرُوا بِهِ وَلِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَلِيَذَّكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (٥٢)).
The Exalted's saying (وَلِيُنْذَرُوا بِهِ): the meaning is: the Qur'an is a communication to the people and for warning; so the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to الْبَلَاغ, or to something omitted if you make لِلنَّاسِ an adjective (ṣifa).
It may also be attached to something omitted, its implied form being "and that they may be warned by it, it was sent down" or "recited". And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الر كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كِتَابٌ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a Book". And «أَنْزَلْنَاهُ» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «كِتَابٌ», not a ḥāl (circumstantial), because «كِتَابًا» is indefinite. (بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ): in the position of the accusative; if you wish, as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "by reason of the permission"; and if you wish, in the position of a ḥāl from «النَّاسَ», i.e. "permitted", or from the agent pronoun, i.e. "being permitted (to do so)". (إِلَى صِرَاطِ): this is a badal (substitute) from His saying «إِلَى النُّورِ», with repetition of the preposition.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَوَيْلٌ لِلْكَافِرِينَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ (٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اللَّهِ الَّذِي): it is read in the genitive as a badal (substitute), and in the nominative on three views:
The first: as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows it as the khabar (predicate). The second: as a khabar, with the mubtadaʾ omitted, i.e. "He is Allah", and «الَّذِي» an adjective (ṣifa). The third: it is a mubtadaʾ, «الَّذِي» its adjective, and the khabar omitted, its implied form being "Allah, to whom belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, is the Almighty, the Praiseworthy"; it was omitted because it had been mentioned before.
And (وَيْلٌ) is a mubtadaʾ, and «لِلْكَافِرِينَ» its khabar.
(مِنْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ): in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «وَيْلٌ», after the khabar, and that is permissible. It may not be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «وَيْلٌ», because of the separation between them by the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِبُّونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَيَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًا أُولَئِكَ فِي ضَلَالٍ بَعِيدٍ (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِبُّونَ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of «الْكَافِرِينَ»; or in the position of the accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» ("I mean"); or in the position of the nominative by an implied «هُمْ» ("they are").
(وَيَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًا): it has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ فَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "except speaking their language".
Among the irregular (shādhdh) readings it was read «بِلِسْنِ قَوْمِهِ», with kasra on the lām and sukūn on the sīn; it means "tongue (language)".
(فَيُضِلُّ) is in the nominative; it was not put in the accusative by conjunction with «لِيُبَيِّنَ», because conjunction makes the meaning of the maʿṭūf (conjoined) like the meaning of what it is conjoined to, and the messengers were sent to make clear, not to lead astray.
Al-Zajjāj said: had it been read in the accusative, with the lām being the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), it would have been permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا أَنْ أَخْرِجْ قَوْمَكَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ أَخْرِجْ قَوْمَكَ): «أَنْ» means «أَيْ» ("that is"), so it has no grammatical position.
It may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); the implied form is then "بِأَنْ أَخْرِجْ" ("with: bring out"); and this has been mentioned in more than one place.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنْجَاكُمْ مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَاءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَاءَكُمْ وَفِي ذَلِكُمْ بَلَاءٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنْجَاكُمْ): it has been mentioned at His saying (إِذْ كُنْتُمْ أَعْدَاءً).
(وَيُذَبِّحُونَ): another ḥāl (circumstantial), conjoined to (يَسُومُونَ).

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ وَلَئِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذَابِي لَشَدِيدٌ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ): conjoined to «إِذْ أَنْجَاكُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعَادٍ وَثَمُودَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ لَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّهُ جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرَدُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِي أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَقَالُوا إِنَّا كَفَرْنَا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ وَإِنَّا لَفِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا تَدْعُونَنَا إِلَيْهِ مُرِيبٍ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَوْمِ نُوحٍ): a badal (substitute) from «الَّذِينَ».
(وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ): conjoined to it; on this view His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ». It may also be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and likewise «جَاءَتْهُمْ».
It may also be that «وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ» its khabar (predicate); or (that «لَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ» is) a ḥāl from the "being settled" (al-istiqrār), and «جَاءَتْهُمُ» is the khabar.
(فِي أَفْوَاهِهِمْ): «فِي» has its usual meaning, an adverb (ẓarf) of «رَدُّوا»; and it is figurative, because when they silenced them, it was as though they put their hands in their mouths and thereby prevented them from speaking.
It is also said: it means «إِلَى» ("to"); and it is also said: it means the bāʾ ("with").

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَتْ رُسُلُهُمْ أَفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَدْعُوكُمْ لِيَغْفِرَ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُؤَخِّرَكُمْ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى قَالُوا إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَصُدُّونَا عَمَّا كَانَ يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُنَا فَأْتُونَا بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ): («شَكٌّ» is) the agent (fāʿil) of the adverbial phrase, because it relies on the hamza (of interrogation).
(فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ): an adjective (ṣifa) or a badal (substitute).
(لِيَغْفِرَ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ): the object is omitted, and «مِنْ» (with its noun) is an adjective of it, i.e. "something of your sins". According to al-Akhfash «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida).
Some of them said: «مِنْ» is for substitution (badal), i.e. "that He may forgive you in place of the punishment of your sins", as in His saying (أَرَضِيتُمْ بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ).
(تُرِيدُونَ): another adjective of «بَشَرٌ».

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَتْ لَهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ إِنْ نَحْنُ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَمُنُّ عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ بِسُلْطَانٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ): («أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ» is) the noun of «كَانَ», and «لَنَا» is the khabar (predicate).
And (إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); it has been mentioned at the beginning of the sūra.
It may also be that the khabar is «بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ», and «لَنَا» is for clarification (tabyīn).

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا لَنَا أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَانَا سُبُلَنَا وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ عَلَى مَا آذَيْتُمُونَا وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ): i.e. "in that we should not rely".
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "not relying". It has been mentioned in more than one place.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاسْتَفْتَحُوا وَخَابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاسْتَفْتَحُوا): it is also read irregularly in the form of the imperative (وَاسْتَفْتِحُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ وَيَأْتِيهِ الْمَوْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ وَمَا هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ وَمِنْ وَرَائِهِ عَذَابٌ غَلِيظٌ (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَتَجَرَّعُهُ): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of «مَاءٍ», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يُسْقَى», or resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَرَمَادٍ اشْتَدَّتْ بِهِ الرِّيحُ فِي يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ لَا يَقْدِرُونَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا عَلَى شَيْءٍ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلَالُ الْبَعِيدُ (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "among what is recited to you is the parable of those who…".
And (أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَرَمَادٍ) is a resumptive clause explaining the parable. It is also said: the clause is the khabar of «مَثَلُ» according to the meaning. It is also said: «مَثَلُ» is a mubtadaʾ, and «أَعْمَالُهُمْ» its khabar, i.e. "their parable is the parable of their deeds"; and «كَرَمَادٍ» on this view is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are like ashes".
[Translator's note: the source reads «أَوْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ» ("or «أَعْمَالُهُمْ»") here, as written; the sense requires "and".]
It is also said: «أَعْمَالُهُمْ» is a badal (substitute) from «مَثَلُ», and «كَرَمَادٍ» is the khabar. Were it outside the Qurʾān, it would be permissible to make «أَعْمَالِهِمْ» a badal from «الَّذِينَ», and that would be a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).
(فِي يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ): (i.e. "its wind is stormy"); then «الرِّيحُ» was omitted and the adjective was given to the day figuratively. It is also said: the implied form is "on a day possessing storminess", so it is by way of relation (nasab), as in their saying نَابِلٌ ("possessor of arrows") and رَامِحٌ ("possessor of a spear").
It was also read «يَوْمِ عَاصِفٍ» with the genitive construct, i.e. "on the day of a stormy wind".
(لَا يَقْدِرُونَ): resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَأْتِ بِخَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ): it is read irregularly with sukūn on the rāʾ in continuous speech (أَلَمْ تَرْ), on the basis that he treated it like the pause.
(خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ): it is read in the form of the past verb, and (خَالِقُ) on the pattern fāʿil; it refers to the past, so it becomes definite by the genitive construct.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا فَقَالَ الضُّعَفَاءُ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعًا فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُغْنُونَ عَنَّا مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ قَالُوا لَوْ هَدَانَا اللَّهُ لَهَدَيْنَاكُمْ سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْنَا أَجَزِعْنَا أَمْ صَبَرْنَا مَا لَنَا مِنْ مَحِيصٍ (٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَبَعًا): if you wish, you may make it the plural of تَابِعٌ ("follower"), like خَادِمٌ and خَدَمٌ, غَائِبٌ and غَيَبٌ; and if you wish, you may make it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of تَبِعَ; the maṣdar is then in the position of the active participle, or the implied form is "possessors of following".
(مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it is originally an adjective (ṣifa) of «شَيْءٍ», its implied form being "مِنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ", with «مِنْ» redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "anything being of the punishment of Allah"; and the verb is construed according to the meaning, its implied form being "will you ward off anything from us?". It may also be that «شَيْءٍ» stands in the position of the maṣdar, i.e. "any availing"; then «مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مُغْنُونَ».
